sections.h2: What is Parkland like for a seller?
sections.html:
Parkland occupies the far northwest edge of Broward, and its buyers tend to want acreage, quiet streets and newer construction. City materials describe a span from State Road 7 in the east to the Everglades in the west, with the Sawgrass Expressway to the south and Loxahatchee Road to the north.

Parkland was founded in 1963 by a cattle farmer who bought more than 1,000 acres of Everglades land with his father and parceled out plots from his ranch. Early buyers could get five acres for as little as $15,000. Roads stayed unpaved until the 1980s and the first traffic light did not arrive until the 1990s, which explains why parts of the city still feel rural. The city says it grew from under 100 residents and 420 acres to nearly 38,000 residents and more than 8,000 acres.

In practice, many lots are large, some properties sit on equestrian or trail corridors, and the age and style of homes vary a lot from one neighborhood to the next. Investors paying cash tend to focus on roof, drainage and permit history rather than finishes, so collect those records first.

sections.h2: Which sale routes fit a Parkland owner?
sections.html:
A Parkland owner can choose a brokered listing, an owner-run sale or a direct cash purchase. Time and repair budget usually decide among them.

  • Brokered listing: the widest buyer pool, with prep work, showings and a wait on the buyer's financing.
  • Private sale: you skip the commission but handle pricing, contract and disclosures yourself.
  • Direct cash purchase: quicker and as-is, with the price reflecting repair and resale risk.

Compare offers on what you actually net after repairs, taxes, fees and carrying costs, and read any contract before you sign. A Parkland house with a newer roof and clean permits will draw stronger bids on every route.

Building permits and occupancy certificates come from the Building Department inside City Hall at 6600 University Drive, phone 954.753.5447. Its page shows a Monday to Thursday schedule, 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

The city moved permitting to a new online portal, and the page tells contractors to re-register and submit fresh insurance and license documents. Permit fees were adjusted beginning October 1, 2025 under a city resolution, so ask the department for the current schedule if you plan repairs before selling.

Unclosed permits for old roof, window or addition work can delay a closing, so ask the department what it has on file for your lot before marketing the house.

sections.h2: How do property taxes affect a Parkland seller?
sections.html:
The state writes the schedule and Broward collects. Valuation happens each January 1, exemption filings close March 1, and the bill lands in November.

  • Paying early earns a sliding discount that starts at 4 percent for November and shrinks by one point each month until February.
  • April 1 is when an unpaid bill becomes delinquent.
  • Up to $50,000 of homestead exemption is available on a permanent residence, with the home occupied that way on January 1.

After a sale, the property is reassessed at full full just value in the following January, so a buyer may owe far more than you do. Do not quote your own bill to a buyer. Broward's appraiser office publishes 954-357-6830 as its number.

sections.h2: What are the deed transfer charges?
sections.html:
A documentary stamp tax applies to deeds, at one rate across Broward. Whoever agrees to pay in the contract, every party to the deed stays liable under the state's rule.

Florida deed and recording charges as printed by the state
ItemRate as printedSource
Deed doc stamps$0.70 per $100 of price paidFla. Stat. 201.02
Mortgage doc stamps35 cents per $100 securedDOR page
Clerk recording, first page$5.00, then $4.00 per added pageFla. Stat. 28.24
Added names beyond four$1.00 eachFla. Stat. 28.24

The clerk takes payment at recording. A written estimate from your closing agent will apply these rates to your actual price.

sections.h2: What if the Parkland house is inherited or behind on payments?
sections.html:
Both have set legal steps. A smaller estate may use summary administration, which the statute opens up at a $150,000 non-exempt ceiling or when two years have passed since death.

In foreclosure, a judgment schedules the auction roughly three to five weeks out unless the lender agrees to a later date. Sale proceeds above the debt may be claimable, and the judgment tells homestead owners to ask the clerk within 10 days. Selling beforehand can protect equity, so talk to an attorney and the lender.

  • Collect the deed, your latest tax bill and lender correspondence.
  • Ask the clerk's office in Broward which filings touch the property.
  • Get a payoff statement before you compare offers.

sections.h2: What if a Parkland tax bill is not paid?
sections.html:
An unpaid bill goes delinquent April 1, and by June 1 the county sells certificates on what remains. A certificate holder may file for a tax deed once two years have passed since April 1 of the issue year, with an application fee of $75.

The tax collector then lists the people who must be noticed, including the titleholder, lienholders and any contract for deed buyer. If you are behind, selling before a deed application is filed keeps options open. Request a current payoff figure from the Broward tax collector's office.

  • Homestead owners over 65 may be able to defer part of the bill with Form DR-570 by March 31.
  • Installment prepayment requires an application by May 1.
  • Partial payments are at the collector's discretion.

sections.h2: Can an unlisted family transfer or quitclaim help me sell in Parkland?
sections.html:
A quitclaim is a taxable document under the DOR list, and it counts as a change of ownership for Save Our Homes unless an exception such as a spouse transfer applies. A transfer to a relative before sale can raise the property's tax base and add stamp tax.

A lady bird deed has its own treatment under a DOR advisement, which says it does not transfer a present beneficial interest on the facts presented. Talk to an attorney before recording anything.

sections.h2: Which Parkland amenities do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
The city's history page counts 11 parks with trails for families, dogs and horses, a library, and a Native American midden more than 1,000 years old. Another city page counts nine parks and five public schools and notes a WalletHub ranking as the best city in Florida to raise a family.

Early residents opened the first library in a concession stand at Quigley Park, and volunteers staffed the first fire organization. Trails and horse access suit buyers who want room, so mention them if your property backs onto one. Check park and school boundaries yourself before advertising them.

sections.h2: What about tenants in a Parkland rental?
sections.html:
Unpaid rent calls for a written 3 day demand, counting no weekends or court holidays. Other fixable lease problems allow a 7 day cure.

A month by month tenancy needs 30 days' notice to end. Before selling an occupied home, read the lease, because the sale alone does not cancel it.

faqs.q: Which office runs the tax timeline for a Parkland home?
faqs.a: Florida writes the timeline and Broward offices apply it. January 1 fixes value, March 1 closes exemption filing, November brings bills, and April 1 starts delinquency.

faqs.q: Does paying cash remove doc stamp tax in Parkland?
faqs.a: No. The DOR page prices deed stamps at $0.70 per $100 paid, and every party to the deed is liable whoever agrees to cover it. Settle who pays in the contract.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Parkland house with open permits?
faqs.a: Yes, though it adds friction. Call the city's Building Department at 954.753.5447 to learn what remains open on your lot, since buyers and title companies will check.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It ends when you sell. Homestead is lost once the home is no longer your permanent residence, and the buyer is assessed at just value starting the following January.

faqs.q: How soon can an inherited Parkland house be sold?
faqs.a: It depends on the court path. Summary administration is available for non-exempt estates up to $150,000, and larger or contested estates take formal administration, so speak with a probate attorney.
